keyChanges.title: Tesla cuts AI5/AI6 memory for DRAM volume, then lifts AI5 only to 96GB
keyChanges.description: On Oct 1, 2026 Elon Musk said Tesla cut RAM in half on AI5, to 72GB of LPDDR5, and by a third on AI6, to 144GB of LPDDR6. He called that 'the only way to get enough volume for Optimus production,' said it 'greatly reduces cost,' and claimed a 'negligible effect' on Optimus because 'memory bandwidth is a bigger limiting factor than total memory storage (bandwidth was held constant).' About 12 hours later, on Oct 2, he walked AI5 up to 96GB so Tesla would not be 'the only company using the min RAM version of LP5.' The settled spec is still about one-third below the 144GB AI5 plan implied by the half-cut, and AI6 stays at 144GB versus an implied ~216GB plan. This is a procurement de-spec before volume production, not evidence that scaling is on track. Musk was replying to a ~200GB-per-humanoid estimate; 96GB is well under that, and the performance claim is untested. Samsung Taylor trial production and a 2027 volume target were already the baseline and did not move. No new AI6 tape-out date, yield, sample shipment, or vehicle-computer allocation was published this window.

positive_signals: Musk says bandwidth was held constant and expects a negligible Optimus performance hit
AI5 was lifted off the 72GB minimum LPDDR5 bin to 96GB within a day, avoiding a Tesla-only low-spec DRAM SKU
96GB AI5 and 144GB AI6 are still far above AI4's 32GB GDDR6 board total
Musk says the smaller configs cut cost and are what makes Optimus unit volume possible
negative_signals: Musk said the cut was the only way to get enough memory for Optimus volume, so the binding constraint is DRAM supply
Settled AI5 at 96GB is still about 33% below the prior 144GB plan; the 72GB figure was not a stable design
AI6 remains cut by a third, to 144GB of LPDDR6
96GB is well under the ~200GB DRAM-per-humanoid estimate Musk was responding to
The 'negligible effect' claim is an assertion, not a measured result
No change to 2027 mass production or Tesla shipments; Taylor trial production does not mean chips in cars or robots
The DRAM configuration was still being revised after tape-out and after Taylor trial production had already started

key_metrics.actual: AI5 settled at 96GB LPDDR5; AI6 at 144GB LPDDR6
key_metrics.target: AI5 plan implied by the half-cut was 144GB; AI6 plan implied by the one-third cut was about 216GB
key_metrics.trajectory: spec reduced before volume; mass production still 2027

keyChanges.title: Berlin cell lead: 4680 still uneconomic, 18 GWh still a 2027 target
keyChanges.description: On October 2, Battery-News published an interview with Robert Meyer, Cell Factory Lead at Tesla Manufacturing Brandenburg. He said Grünheide is still planned to start its own 4680 production in 2027 and ramp to as much as 18 GWh a year. That is the same Construction-phase target already on the books, not current output, yield, or a pulled-forward start. Meyer said that from a pure cost perspective the step 'offers limited advantages' and that it is currently hardly possible to manufacture cells economically in Europe, citing no EU output-based cell incentive and no Asian-style local cell ecosystem. Dry electrode remains the planned process, with claimed cuts to footprint, capex, and solvent recovery, but Berlin has no disclosed yield. He also said the Texas 4680 complexity challenge is 'already solved' and will transfer to Grünheide. Nothing in this window added a Texas GWh, yield, scrap, or cost figure; the last official frame is still the Q2 10 GWh Early Ramp. Tesla still intends to hire more than 1,500 people for cell manufacturing and does not require prior cell experience. A November 23 Gigafactory visit tied to the interview is of vehicle production, not a cell-line start. This is a strategic commitment, not evidence the line is scaling.

positive_signals: Tesla is not cancelling Grünheide cell manufacturing; Meyer frames it as a resilience and vertical-integration choice
Dry electrode remains the stated Berlin 4680 process, which Tesla says cuts energy, footprint, and solvent-recovery cost
Named plan to add more than 1,500 cell-manufacturing employees, with internal training for people who have not made cells before
negative_signals: No Berlin 4680 cells are in production; start is still 2027 and up to 18 GWh is a ceiling, not a run-rate
Meyer says the pure cost case offers limited advantages and that economic cell manufacturing in Europe is currently hardly possible
No new yield, scrap, cost-per-kWh, or installed-output number for Berlin or Texas
The claim that Texas has already solved 4680 complexity is not backed by a new production figure; Texas cathode remains the Q2 10 GWh Early Ramp
The 1,500 hires are still ahead, and Meyer says experienced European cell talent is scarce
The November 23 site look is vehicle production, not cell output

key_metrics.actual: Berlin 4680 not producing; Texas still last framed as Q2 10 GWh Early Ramp
key_metrics.target: Grünheide own 4680 cells starting 2027, up to 18 GWh/year
key_metrics.trajectory: Plan unchanged and still pre-production; Tesla's cell lead says Europe cell economics do not work today

keyChanges.title: Tesla's 300-plus Austin Cybercab claim tracks the registry, not verified rides
keyChanges.description: On Oct 10, 2026 Tesla's Robotaxi account said it had scaled to "300+ Cybercabs serving Austin," an "8x increase in 30 days." Ashok Elluswamy added that the cabs are "everywhere in Austin now" and "Dallas soon," with no date. That 300-plus figure sits on the Texas automated-vehicle authorization list, not a dispatch census. Robotaxi Tracker's TxDMV feed (https://robotaxitracker.com) showed 319 Cybercabs and 420 Model Ys authorized as of Oct 10, 739 combined, after a 150-Cybercab batch on Oct 9 lifted the company total from 589. Tesla's earlier posts matched that same list (Cybercab #67 on Sept 21; 69 Cybercabs and 420 Model Ys on Sept 24). An 8x jump to 300 implies a base near 38, but the roster was already 126 Cybercabs on Sept 26. The same tracker snapshot matched only 193 of Tesla's 739 authorized vehicles to an active community record (368 with any community match, 371 unmatched). A same-day EV write-up of the tracker's Austin sighting directory, which it calls a floor, put observed unsupervised Austin vehicles near 105 Cybercabs and 170 Model Ys — about 2.5x Cybercab sightings in 30 days, and about 11% of logged Austin trips in Cybercabs. Paid Cybercab rides are still Austin-only. Dozens of Cybercabs filled the Dallas robotaxi hub on Oct 8 while Dallas riders still get Model Ys, and a drone observer estimated roughly 190–200 Cybercabs at the Houston lot on Oct 6, some leaving onto public roads, with no announced passenger service. Tesla has not said how many of the "300+" are in paid service at once, whether monitors are still aboard, or when Dallas rides start.

positive_signals: Tesla's Robotaxi account publicly claimed 300+ Cybercabs serving Austin on Oct 10, and Ashok Elluswamy named Dallas as next
Texas authorization for Cybercabs rose from 126 on Sept 26 to 319 by Oct 10 (420 Model Ys unchanged; 739 combined), so hardware is being credentialed
Cybercabs are physically staged in Dallas and an observer estimated ~190–200 at the Houston lot, with some Houston test driving on public roads
negative_signals: Prior Robotaxi-account fleet lines matched the TxDMV list exactly, so 'serving Austin' is not an independent in-service count
8x does not survive the Sept 26 base of 126 authorized Cybercabs; registered growth since early September is closer to 6.5x and sightings closer to 2.5x
Robotaxi Tracker matched only 193 of 739 authorized Tesla vehicles to an active community record
EV's reading of the Austin sighting floor was ~105 Cybercabs versus the 300+ claim, and only ~11% of logged Austin trips were Cybercabs
Paid Cybercab service is still Austin-only; Dallas is 'soon' with no date and Houston has no launch
Tesla has not said whether the claimed 300+ still use safety monitors or how many are carrying riders at once

keyChanges.title: NHTSA gave Tesla until Oct 30, not Nov 20, for sworn Cybercab FMVSS answers
keyChanges.description: NHTSA's Sept 29, 2026 memo to file in audit query AQ26002 says Tesla asked on Sept 18 for an eight-week extension, to Nov 20, to answer the Sept 10 Special Order on how it self-certified a Cybercab with no steering wheel, brake pedal, or mirrors. NHTSA granted 30 days on Sept 22. Answers that were due Sept 30 are now due Oct 30, nine days after Q3 earnings. Tesla told the agency it needed time because of the volume of the request and a privilege review. The order's 21 items include which standards Tesla certified to, whether temporary driver controls were fitted and then removed, and how the car meets FMVSS 135, which says the service brake shall be activated by a foot control. NHTSA also asks how the car complies at all without a Part 555 exemption. The opening audit estimated about 1,000 vehicles. The memo does not find a violation and does not pause Austin service. A incomplete or untruthful response can draw civil penalties of up to $27,874 a day. Tesla still has not published the sworn answers, so a wider Cybercab release is still sitting on an open certification question.

positive_signals: NHTSA did not shut down Austin Cybercab service when it moved the deadline
The agency has not issued a finding that the Cybercab fails a safety standard
negative_signals: Tesla missed the original Sept 30 sworn-answer date
NHTSA refused the Nov 20 date Tesla asked for and set Oct 30 instead
The sharpest open question is FMVSS 135's foot-brake rule and the lack of a Part 555 exemption
Tesla's own extension request cited the volume of records still to search, so the certification file was not ready
Daily penalties apply if the Oct 30 response is incomplete or untruthful, and nothing public explains the pedal-less design yet

keyChanges.title: Austin robotaxi hours move only to 11 p.m. because night vision still misses pets
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account said Austin service now runs until 11 p.m., one hour past the 6 a.m.–10 p.m. window it has used since Aug 26. Elon Musk posted on Oct 3 that the constraint is "making sure that we don't run over pets when they're hard to see at night," specifically "grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark." He gave no date for hours past 11 p.m. or for 24/7 service. TeslaNorth's write-up of the Oct 3 CNBC piece, which could not be opened directly, also reported rider complaints of long waits and wrong-place pickups and drop-offs, plus an Austin Fire captain who wants authority to move or shut down an autonomous vehicle. Musk's reply was that Tesla is "being extremely careful with autonomous safety," not that those gaps are closed. One extra evening hour does not remove the night-perception ceiling.

positive_signals: Austin robotaxi availability did lengthen by one hour, to 11 p.m., and Tesla stated the change on its Robotaxi account
Musk named a specific perception failure mode instead of offering a vague timeline
negative_signals: Service is still not overnight; the cutoff only moved from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m.
Musk said low-contrast pets at night are the main unsolved limiter, with no date for a further extension
TeslaNorth's account of CNBC described long waits, bad pickup and drop-off locations, and no public-safety remote shutdown authority
Musk's 'extremely careful' reply does not schedule monitor removal or 24/7 operation

keyChanges.title: Driverless robotaxis still need a person to plug them in at a public Supercharger
keyChanges.description: On Oct 3 an observer at an Austin Supercharger filmed one empty Cybercab and nine empty Model Y robotaxis arrive with nobody aboard. A Tesla employee plugged each car in and moved vehicles that had parked too poorly to charge. Teslarati wrote the session up on Oct 5 as leftover "scrappy DNA" while wireless charging is still a patent and an FCC waiver, not equipment in the fleet. The cars can deadhead without a driver. They still cannot replenish themselves. A human at a public stall is the charging plan a month after paid Cybercab rides began, and it does not scale with a claimed 300-car Austin fleet.

positive_signals: At least some Cybercab and Model Y robotaxis deadheaded to a public Supercharger with no one in the car
One attendant charged a batch of vehicles, so the workaround functions at small scale
negative_signals: Charging is still manual plug-in plus a human repositioning poorly parked cars
The session was at a public Supercharger, not an automated robotaxi depot
Wireless charging is not deployed; Teslarati points only to ongoing patent work
The observation is a single site visit, but it is the operating method Tesla is using, not a demo

keyChanges.title: Croatia Recognises Dutch FSD Supervised Approval, Eighth EU State
keyChanges.description: On 29 September 2026 Tesla Europe said FSD Supervised was approved in Croatia and that rollout would begin soon, which Tesla North, Croatia Week and a Reuters report treated as the eighth European recognition of the Dutch provisional approval. By 8–10 October Tesla’s European Assisted Driving pages still listed exactly eight countries: the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia and Croatia. This is the same Article 39 mutual-recognition path as Czechia, not an EU-wide homologation and not unsupervised autonomy. Heise’s 6 October legal recap of states that had notified RDW still stopped at Czechia and about 12 percent of the EU population, and no Croatian ministry decision was published in the sources read here. Croatia adds roughly four million people and does not move the file near the qualified-majority bar of 15 states and 65 percent of the population. Rollout was still described as upcoming, not complete.

positive_signals: Tesla Europe announced Croatian approval on 29 September and said rollout would begin soon
Reuters and Croatia Week reported Croatia had joined the supervised-FSD countries
Tesla’s own European pages, as checked by Tesla North on 8 and 10 October, list Croatia among eight live countries
negative_signals: No Croatian authority document was found; the public record starts with Tesla’s announcement
Heise on 6 October still counted seven notifying states and about 12 percent of EU population, ending at Czechia
Supervised provisional recognition only; a driver remains responsible and the EU vote is still outstanding
Croatia does not materially change the 65 percent population threshold for a qualified majority

keyChanges.title: Germany Will Lobby for EU FSD Approval, But Has Not Granted It
keyChanges.description: On 6 October Germany’s Federal Ministry of Transport said minister Steffen Bilger had reached a September understanding with Tesla and would push for a timely Europe-wide approval. The ministry called the FSD name misleading, said Tesla had offered to rename the system Tesla Assisted Driving, and said both sides agreed the assistant may exceed the posted limit by at most 10 percent. The driver stays 100 percent responsible. That is political support for the EU procedure, not a KBA approval: Germany is still absent from Tesla’s live-country list, and as of 10 October the mandatory tutorial appears to have been filmed in Berlin, where owners cannot switch the system on. The same day Bilger told a Tagesspiegel Background conference, via dpa and Heise, that if an EU deal fails Germany would discuss what it can do alone. Heise identifies that fallback as Article 39(5), limited to Germany and lapsing six months after a Commission rejection. The 6 October TCMV meeting discussed the file and did not vote; a decision is not expected before December. KBA still wants to test a car itself and has given no end date. By 8 October most, but not all, Tesla Europe sites had switched the marketing name; Tesla has not confirmed an in-car rename or that the 10 percent cap is actually in the software.

positive_signals: Transport minister Bilger publicly committed to pushing a timely EU-wide approval after September talks
Ministry and Tesla agreed a maximum 10 percent speed offset, which Berlin says it will support in the EU process
Tesla began replacing the FSD name with Tesla Assisted Driving on most European websites by 8 October
A national Article 39(5) path was at least discussed if Brussels does not act
negative_signals: Germany has not approved use on its own roads; KBA review and a vehicle test have no published deadline
The 6 October TCMV sitting produced discussion only; the next chance is December at the earliest
The ministry itself says the Full Self-Driving name is misleading and that this is driver assistance, not autonomy
The 10 percent overspeed allowance is a concession to a known speeding problem, not evidence the behavior is fixed
Headlines that Germany gave a green light or approved FSD overstate a lobbying pledge
Eight recognitions remain near 12 to 13 percent of EU population, far from 15 states and 65 percent
Any German-only approval could lapse six months after a later Commission rejection

keyChanges.title: Reuters: Tesla Pressed RDW to Narrow the FSD Review
keyChanges.description: A 7 October Reuters investigation, reported in detail by InsideEVs and summarized by Slovak daily Pravda, says Tesla pressed Dutch type-approval authority RDW to limit the cost and intensity of the FSD Supervised review and rallied owners to email regulators that delays would cost lives. Reuters reviewed internal emails and spoke with seven traffic-safety researchers. They said Tesla’s April evidence dashboard relied on behavioral surrogates — horn use, sudden acceleration and braking, turn-signal use, automatic emergency braking — rather than crash outcomes, covered far fewer miles than Tesla’s consumer fleet, and did not show that FSD prevents fatal crashes. InsideEVs reports that after Tesla complained, an RDW staffer offered to discuss ways to adjust or reduce the required scrutiny. RDW told Reuters those exchanges are routine and do not compromise independence. The same Dutch file is what the other EU states are recognizing one by one. France and the Nordics remain cautious on speed and attention. This does not reverse the approvals already granted, but it undercuts the claim that the exported safety case is independently settled.

positive_signals: RDW said manufacturer exchanges are a normal part of assessment and do not reduce independence
Heise separately reports RDW logged more than 3,000 test hours, more than 1,000 of its own runs, and monthly rather than annual reporting
negative_signals: Seven researchers told Reuters the surrogate metrics are poor proxies and do not demonstrate fatal-crash prevention
Tesla’s dossier covered far fewer miles than the consumer fleet and was not an independent peer-reviewed study
Internal emails reportedly show Tesla pushing RDW to shrink the review, and a staffer offering to discuss reducing scrutiny
Tesla and fans framed regulatory delay as costing lives, including dozens of emails to Swedish and Norwegian officials
The Reuters body itself was not readable here (401); findings rely on InsideEVs’ account and Pravda’s summary of the same investigation

keyChanges.title: Slovakia Promises an FSD Recognition Letter, Has Not Sent It
keyChanges.description: On 7 October Slovak transport minister Jozef Ráž said in a video that his ministry had been talking with Tesla and would within days send the Netherlands the letter recognizing RDW’s provisional FSD Supervised approval. Pravda reported on 8 October that this would make Slovakia the ninth EU country if the letter is actually delivered, and Reuters headlined that Slovakia is to approve the system. The minister also said the driver does not hand over responsibility. As of 10 October Tesla’s country list was still eight states, with no Slovak activation. Ráž made the announcement just before municipal elections in which he is running for mayor of Bratislava. No date for the letter, no Slovak road test, and no eligible-fleet figure were disclosed.

positive_signals: The transport minister, not a Tesla fan account, said a recognition letter to RDW is the planned next step
Pravda and Reuters both reported the intention, and the minister restated that supervision stays with the driver
negative_signals: The letter had not been confirmed sent by 10 October, and Tesla’s live list still omitted Slovakia
Announcement landed immediately before local elections in which the minister is a Bratislava mayoral candidate
No independent Slovak test program was described; this would be another paperwork recognition of the Dutch file
It does not create an EU-wide approval, which is still not expected before December

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.11 and HW3 v14.3 Lite roll out on 2026.33.5 with unchanged notes
keyChanges.description: Tesla started an early-access rollout of supervised FSD v14.3.11 for HW4 and FSD v14.3 Lite for HW3 on firmware 2026.33.5 on Oct 7. Tesla Oracle (Oct 8) says the v14.3.11 notes are the same as the previous version and that TeslaFi/Tessie then showed the build on under 1% of the fleet, limited at first to the early-access group. Not a Tesla App's 2026.33.5 notes match the v14.3.10 text on 2026.27.11 bullet for bullet, including pothole avoidance still listed under Upcoming Improvements, and the v14.3 Lite section repeats the v14.2 Lite bullets (distillation from HW4 v14, parking/reversing, arrival options, speed profiles) for HW3 Model 3 and Y only, not Model S/X. By Oct 10 that tracker showed 311 cars and 2.5% of its fleet on 2026.33.5. A Black Tesla early clip from New York reported one ~25-minute loop with no intervention and easier unprotected left turns; that is a single early-access drive, not a measured gain. The v14.3.9 false camera-service alert is still not documented as fixed. This is not v15.

positive_signals: HW4 v14.3.11 and HW3 Model 3/Y v14.3 Lite began installing together on 2026.33.5 on Oct 7
TeslaFi count on 2026.33.5 rose from under 1% on Oct 8 to 311 cars / 2.5% by Oct 10
One early-access NYC drive reported no intervention and smoother unprotected left turns
negative_signals: Published v14.3.11 notes are identical to v14.3.10, including the same upcoming-pothole line
v14.3 Lite notes copy v14.2 Lite and the package lists HW3 Model 3 and Y only, not S/X
False camera-service alerts from v14.3.9 are still absent from the changelog
Customer stack remains supervised v14; v15 is not in this build

keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.12 shows up on 2026.38.5 with the same notes and almost no installs
keyChanges.description: Not a Tesla App listed firmware 2026.38.5 on Oct 10 as FSD Supervised 14.3.12 for North American HW4. The v14.3.12 changelog is the same text as v14.3.11 and v14.3.10: RL and vision-encoder upgrades, the MLIR runtime claim, parking and small-animal bullets, and upcoming items still limited to broader reasoning and pothole avoidance. TeslaFi on that page showed 0% of the tracked fleet and about 2 installs. The wider 2026.38 branch (2026.38 at 7.4% and 2026.38.3.1 at 7.8% on the same tracker) is the Halloween, visuals, and map wave and does not carry a new FSD version. No second outlet had a v14.3.12 writeup on Oct 10. Treat this as a same-notes point release that has not actually propagated, not as a new model.

positive_signals: A newer HW4 label, v14.3.12, is attached to firmware 2026.38.5 dated Oct 10
negative_signals: Release notes are unchanged from v14.3.10 and v14.3.11
TeslaFi showed about 2 installs and 0% of the tracked fleet
The broad 2026.38 rollout is not this FSD build
Only Not a Tesla App's tracker documents v14.3.12 so far

keyChanges.title: Musk says night pet detection is still unsolved; no FSD v15 in customer OTAs
keyChanges.description: On Oct 3 Elon Musk said the main thing Tesla is still solving is not running over pets that are hard to see at night, specifically grey kittens on grey tarmac, and that robotaxi operating hours moved only from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m. Teslarati reports that a shift to 24/7 robotaxi operation is tied to FSD v15 on robotaxi vehicles and was described as expected this month, and that the night edge case is not validated. Musk did not say the pet work is the v15 release itself. Through Oct 10 the newest customer labels on Not a Tesla App are supervised v14.3.11 and v14.3.12. Their small-animal bullet is carried forward from v14.3.10 and does not show a solved low-light case. October is not finished, but no tracked customer OTA is v15, so the month's 24/7 software step is not in evidence. Fleet size and city hours belong to robotaxi operations; this item is only the software ship status.

positive_signals: Musk restated that vision-only photon-count processing is still the intended night solution, not extra sensors
v14.3.x notes continue to claim extra RL training on small animals
negative_signals: Musk named low-contrast night pets as the open problem on Oct 3, after v14.3.10 was already out
Service time moved one hour, to 11 p.m., not to overnight
No v15 build is in the customer OTA tracker as of Oct 10; newest labels are v14.3.11 and v14.3.12
The October robotaxi v15 / 24/7 step has no software release to point to yet

keyChanges.title: Pothole avoidance and route memory stay promised, not in v14.3.11 or v14.3.12
keyChanges.description: On Oct 1 Tesla AI principal engineer Phil Duan replied on X that improvements are coming for both pothole avoidance and navigation routing, after a driver called those the remaining pain points on v14.3.10. Not a Tesla App (Oct 2) read that as upcoming pothole detection plus route and parking-habit learning from driver interventions, and noted it is unknown whether that lands in a v14 point release or in v15. The builds that followed did not include it: v14.3.11 (Oct 7) and v14.3.12 (Oct 10) still list 'Add pothole avoidance' under Upcoming Improvements, the same line carried since the v14.3 notes. A Teslarati owner column around Oct 6 still describes potholes, abrupt bumps, speed-limit misses, and bad neighborhood routing as reasons supervised FSD needs takeovers, and says Tesla has improvements coming rather than shipped.

positive_signals: A Tesla AI engineer publicly confirmed on Oct 1 that pothole and routing fixes are in progress
The described route memory would extend Preferred Routes using interventions and parking habits
negative_signals: Pothole avoidance is still an upcoming bullet in v14.3.11 and v14.3.12, not a shipped behavior
The same upcoming line has sat in v14.3 notes since the spring v14.3 release
No ship date, and the note does not say the work is in v15 versus another point release
Current supervised driving still needs takeovers for potholes, bumps, speed limits, and routing

keyChanges.title: Tesla LinkedIn openings at 8,185; mix still ~41% sales/service, not an AI ramp
keyChanges.description: AltIndex’s live count of Tesla active LinkedIn listings was 8,185 on the 2026-10-10 fetch, up 184 (+2.3%) from the 8,001 print filed for 2026-09-26. The page has no timestamp. An unlabeled 0.6% badge sits next to 8,185 and is not a confirmed day-over-day change. The page’s own headline — “up 445.7% over the past three months” and “hiring acceleration” — describes the earlier ramp (July monthly 3,332, August 5,026, September monthly 7,928), not this two-week window. September’s chart point of 7,928 is a different monthly series and sits below the Sept 26 daily print, so it must not overwrite the daily series. Six-month share is Sales & Delivery 21%, Service & Vehicle 20% (about 41% combined), Supply Chain 11%, Recruiting & People 8%, Engineering 8%, and Autonomy & Robotaxi 6%. That mix is unchanged versus last week’s roughly 40% service/sales, 8% engineering, and 6% autonomy. LinkedIn’s public Tesla company page only shows “8,000+” worldwide and leads with sales and service roles, which corroborates the order of magnitude and the mix. LinkedIn headcount on the same AltIndex page is about 92,621. No Teslarati, TeslaNorth, or Tesla Oracle article in the window reported an AI, FSD, or Optimus engineering hiring wave.

positive_signals: Active LinkedIn listings rose from 8,001 on 2026-09-26 to 8,185 on the 2026-10-10 AltIndex snapshot (+184, +2.3%).
LinkedIn’s public Tesla jobs page still shows 8,000+ openings worldwide, so the tracker is in the right range.
negative_signals: A two-week +2.3% move is not a hiring wave. AltIndex’s +445.7% line is the prior three-month ramp (July 3,332 to the September monthly 7,928), and the September chart point is a different series from the daily count.
Six-month mix is still Sales & Delivery 21% plus Service & Vehicle 20%, versus Engineering 8% and Autonomy & Robotaxi 6% — the same non-AI composition as the Sept 26 filing.
The 0.6% figure beside 8,185 is unlabeled. Tier-1 news searches in the window returned no AI or Optimus engineering hiring story.

keyChanges.title: New Robotaxi and Optimus posts are lot support and data collection, not engineering
keyChanges.description: The visible new volume inside the window is operations staffing. A Tesla Robotaxi Fleet Support Specialist (Night Shift) in Doral, Florida, was posted about five days before the 2026-10-10 fetch (about 2026-10-05), marked entry level and full-time, and still among the first 25 applicants. The posting assigns vehicle inspections, car wash and detailing, lot management, moving and charging vehicles, and logistics coordination. It requires a driver’s license, treats the role as safety-critical with drug testing, and says overtime is typical. The same title, across day, afternoon, and night shifts, was listed in the past one to two weeks in many other U.S. cities on LinkedIn search cards (including Orlando, Tampa, Miami, Austin, El Paso, and others). Those city cards were not each opened, and LinkedIn’s “602 Robotaxi Fleet Support jobs” past-month total is unusable because the result page mixes unrelated Tesla roles. On the Optimus side, a Lead Training Coordinator in Austin (posted about two days before the fetch, mid-senior, Mon–Fri 10:00–18:30) owns onboarding and certification for data-collection operators, and a Data Auditor Supervisor in Fremont (about four days before the fetch, $92,000–$138,000 plus cash and stock, same weekday shift) leads auditors who check recordings and metadata before Optimus data is consumed. Both are data-ops leadership, not robotics design or ML research. A few Palo Alto software titles (Robotaxi & Optimus fullstack/distributed systems, and a Digital Optimus realtime-games ML role) appeared on search cards in the past week; those pages were not opened and do not amount to an engineering wave. This is a hiring-composition signal. It is not a robotaxi fleet-size or Optimus production update.

positive_signals: Tesla is staffing Robotaxi fleet support across many U.S. cities and adding Optimus data-collection training and audit leads in Austin and Fremont, all posted inside this window.
The Fremont Data Auditor Supervisor lists $92,000–$138,000 plus cash and stock, so the data-ops layer is a real paid program, not a placeholder title.
negative_signals: The opened Doral Robotaxi Fleet Support Specialist role is entry-level shift work: wash, inspect, move, and charge cars. It is not autonomy engineering, which is why Autonomy & Robotaxi can stay at 6% of openings while these posts proliferate.
The opened Optimus roles train and audit data-collection operators. They do not add ML, controls, or actuator design headcount.
LinkedIn’s 602 / 731 / 1,000+ keyword totals for these titles are polluted AI-search counts and cannot be used as a hiring metric.

keyChanges.title: Giga Texas Optimus shell is about 40% steel, not a factory
keyChanges.description: Joe Tegtmeyer’s October 1 Giga Texas flyover, reviewed by Humanoids Daily on October 3, puts roughly 40% of the basic steel structure up at the dedicated Optimus building. Upper-floor concrete is going in on some bays and roofing insulation has started to arrive, but the eastern side and southern half are still footings and grade beams with no steel. That is incremental progress past the mid-September steel-frame photos, not a finished building. Utilities, walls, roof, mechanical systems, and production equipment are still ahead. Tegtmeyer’s “more than 7 million square feet,” late-2027 first output, and ~10 million robots a year are his reading of the plan, not a new Tesla disclosure. BASENOR’s “steel frame nearly done by October” headline overstates the same site. No production line is installed, and Tesla still has not shown Gen 3 or named an external customer.

keyChanges.title: Optimus touch-sensor patent is a 2025 filing, not a working hand
keyChanges.description: USPTO published Tesla application US20260310299A1 on October 8, 2026. Tesla filed it on September 11, 2025, with priority to a provisional from April 4, 2025. It describes flexible capacitive or resistive tactile arrays that can be thermoformed or dispensed onto curved fingers, palms, and a humanoid ‘skin,’ plus manufacturing methods. The filing never names Optimus, gives no sensitivity, durability, pixel count, or cost, and does not say the design is in Gen 3. Headlines that Optimus can now ‘feel objects’ overclaim a publication. It also does not fix The Information’s late-September report that current touch sensors are unreliable enough that Tesla is using a replaceable sensing glove. Publication of an old application is not a hand that can be built at volume.

keyChanges.title: Q3 deliveries of 486,532 beat a low consensus, but volume is still down YoY and the beat is mostly destocking
keyChanges.description: Tesla's October 2 production and delivery release showed 486,532 vehicles delivered and 464,391 produced in Q3 2026. Deliveries beat the September 29 company-compiled consensus of 461,974 (24 analysts) by 24,558, or 5.3%, and rose 1.3% from Q2's 480,126. They were still 2.1% below the Q3 2025 record of 497,099, ending two straight quarters of year-over-year growth. Model 3/Y were 478,237 deliveries and 457,387 produced; other models (Cybertruck, Semi, and leftover S/X) were 8,295 deliveries and 7,004 produced, down 47.9% and about 40% year over year. Deliveries exceeded production by 22,141, so nearly the entire consensus beat came from drawing inventory rather than a higher build rate — production was only about 2,400 units above the delivery consensus. Year-to-date deliveries are 1,324,681, up 8.8% from 1,217,902. Energy storage was 13.7 GWh, up from 12.5 GWh a year ago and 13.5 GWh in Q2, but 2.2 GWh short of the 15.9 GWh consensus and below the 14.2 GWh Q4 2025 record. BYD's passenger BEV sales were 762,478, widening its lead over Tesla to about 276,000 vehicles from about 77,000 in Q2. Full financials are due after the close on October 21.

keyChanges.title: Shanghai wholesale hits a 2026 high of 95,366 while China retail falls for a fourth straight month
keyChanges.description: CPCA preliminary data released October 9 put Tesla China's September wholesale (domestic plus export) at 95,366, up 5.0% year over year and 10.7% from August, the factory's best month of 2026 and the highest since December 2025's 97,171. The mix is not a domestic recovery. China retail deliveries were 64,837, down 9.35% year over year — a fourth consecutive monthly decline — even though they rose 29.6% from August's weak 50,047. Exports were 30,529, up 58.3% year over year but down 15.5% from August. Third-quarter Shanghai wholesale was a record 275,111, equal to about 57% of Tesla's global deliveries, but China retail for the quarter was 142,133, down 16.0% year over year and a sixth straight quarterly decline. Retail in China was 29.2% of global Q3 deliveries, down from 34.1% a year earlier. Through nine months, wholesale is 743,060 (+22.5%), domestic deliveries 381,088 (−11.9%), and exports 361,972 (+108%), so exports are now 48.7% of Shanghai wholesale versus 28.6% a year ago. The September 25 cash discounts through October 31 are still the demand backdrop; CPCA figures are preliminary.

keyChanges.title: September European registrations jump, including a Germany Model Y win, off an easy 2025 base
keyChanges.description: National registration data show a sharp September rebound, concentrated in quarter-end deliveries and markets that were depressed a year ago. Reuters, citing PFA, Mobility Sweden, ANFAC, OFV, and bilstatistik, reported October 1 that Tesla registrations rose 61.9% in France, 38.4% in Sweden, 24.8% in Spain, 2.2% in Norway, and 2.9% in Denmark. ACEA figures it cited put January–August Tesla registrations across the EU, UK, and EFTA up 43.3%, only modestly ahead of the broader BEV market's 38.8%. Germany's KBA numbers, out later in the week, were larger: 8,038 Model Ys (+260.9%), ahead of the VW Golf's 6,580, and 12,552 Teslas overall (+268.7%, 4.9% share). That is only the second month the Model Y has led Germany, and year-to-date it is still second among German EVs behind the Skoda Elroq at 29,464. Spain's Model 3 was the country's best-selling car for the month at 2,528 (+27.9%), but not year-to-date. Model Y also led Norway (4,810, 25.7% share), France (8,183), Sweden (2,330), Denmark, the Netherlands, and Ireland. Norway and Denmark, the most saturated markets, barely grew. Analysts quoted by Reuters flagged easier year-ago comparisons and said 2027 growth should slow toward the overall market as Chinese and European competition widens.

keyChanges.title: Tesla signs $30B of undrawn credit; no 2026 draw and no project earmark
keyChanges.description: On Sept. 29, 2026 Tesla signed three unsecured facilities, disclosed in an SEC filing that Not a Tesla App quoted the next day. The pieces are a $20 billion delayed-draw term loan due Sept. 29, 2029, an $8 billion five-year revolver due Sept. 29, 2031, and a $2 billion 364-day revolver due Sept. 28, 2027. Nothing has been borrowed, and Tesla said it does not plan to draw this year. Up to 10 draws are allowed in the first 18 months. Unused commitments fall to $10 billion after 12 months and $5 billion after 15 months, then expire. Borrowed amounts carry a variable rate, and Tesla must keep at least $5 billion of liquidity under the agreements' definition. Tesla also closed an older undrawn $5 billion revolver that ran to January 2028, with no penalty. The article names Terafab, the Nevada Semi plant, and Optimus as the spending backdrop. The filing does not earmark the capacity to any of them. This is dry powder, not a construction start, a Semi build rate, or an Optimus order.

sentiment.rationale: The facilities are real and committed, but nothing is drawn, Tesla said it will not use them in 2026, and the filing does not fund a named project.

keyChanges.title: Grimes Terafab is still graded earth; $119B is four optional phases
keyChanges.description: Engineering News-Record on Oct. 8, using county and JETI filings plus Oct. 6 drone footage, reported that the Grimes County production site is still earthwork and access roads, not fab buildings. The Anderson-Shiro JETI application, posted June 8 and still the controlling public document, puts that district's Phase 1 eligible investment at about $10.37 billion, with only $123.4 million scheduled for 2026, and labels 2026-2028 as construction. ENR adds the Iola slice to reach the familiar $16.8 billion first phase and describes three later phases of about $38.6 billion, $38.6 billion, and $25.3 billion through 2036. The application itself calls $55 billion to $119 billion a range for up to four phases and says later phases are built only if the applicant decides to proceed. The same Anderson-Shiro table lists zero new operating jobs in 2026, 2027, and 2028, then 617 in 2029 and no further additions through 2035. That is one district's Phase 1 slice, not the 3,000 jobs in the state announcement. ENR also says Tesla is recruiting construction managers in Anderson and that no general contractor, architect, or engineer has been named. Spectrum's Sept. 28 line that SpaceX expects limited operations in late 2027 does not match the JETI construction window or the 2029 jobs start. Neighbors told Spectrum they are already worried about water and electric bills. The filings describe on-site power and Gibbons Creek surface water as the plan, not as permits issued this week. Nothing in this imagery is the Dec. 1 full-construction start.

keyChanges.title: Terafab records defendants still unserved a month after SpaceX sued
keyChanges.description: Spectrum News checked the Travis County docket on Oct. 6 and reported that Attorney General Ken Paxton and Grimes County are still listed as unserved in SpaceX's Sept. 8 suit to block Terafab records. Until they are served, their answer clock has not started. First Amendment attorney Joe Larsen told Spectrum these cases rarely finish in less than a year. Grimes County Citizens for Responsible Development attorney Bill Aleshire said SpaceX has no special right to hide taxpayer records. SpaceX is asking to permanently withhold land purchases, the entire tax-break application, project costs, structural design, and employee contacts, citing trade secrets and competitive harm. The filing itself was already public on Sept. 10. What is new is that a month later the defendants have not been served and the records stay sealed, even though Paxton's office ruled in July that most of the requested material should be released.

keyChanges.description: The Austin American-Statesman reported Oct. 10 that College Station staff have briefed the council on housing, hotels, and roads, using Taylor's Samsung plant and Brownsville's SpaceX boom as warnings.
